title: observability: add token-level cost & latency breakdowns + dashboards and alert tuning
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Provide token-level observability and actionable dashboards to help teams optimize inference cost and latency. Current dashboards show request-level averages which mask hotspot generators (e.g., long context prompts, high-retry code paths) and make it hard to attribute cost to routes/models. This change introduces token-level cost and latency breakdowns, a set of Grafana dashboards for per-route/token-position analysis, tracing spans for token generation phases, and tuned alert thresholds for latency and cost regressions.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds token-level metrics emitted by the serving runtime: token.generate.latency, token.generate.cost, token.cache.hit, token.kv.fetch.latency (all tagged by route, customer_id_hash, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, and token_position_bucket).
- Updates tracing instrumentation to include tokenize->decode->emit spans with token position and batch_id metadata for better root-cause mapping.
- New Grafana dashboard: Observability / Token Cost & Latency which includes heatmaps, percentile curves by token position, per-route cost waterfall, and model-variant filters.
- Adds Prometheus recording rules to compute rolling token-cost-per-minute and token-latency-p95-per-route to avoid heavy cardinality in queries.
- Adds alert rule adjustments: latency p95 increase (auto-tuned baseline) and token-cost-per-minute spike alerts with knock-on suppression to reduce noise.
- Adds documentation and quickstart snippets for integrating the new dashboards into the Console and for interpreting token-level metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] Serve-side metric emission from runtime (C++)
- [x] Tracing span enhancements (service-instrumentation)
- [x] Prometheus recording rules and alert tuning
- [x] Grafana dashboards & panels
- [x] Console integration docs and redwood-docs entry
- [x] Unit tests for telemetry emission and CI integration tests for dashboard provisioning

Notes on implementation:
- To limit cardinality, token_position is bucketed (0-7,8-31,32-127,128+), and seq_len_bucket approximates typical seq lengths. All customer identifiers are hashed to preserve privacy.
- Recording rules compute per-route aggregates at 1m and 5m resolutions; raw token metrics are emitted at high throughput but not retained long-term except via recording rules.
- Alert tuning uses an automatically computed baseline (rolling 7d median) and triggers when p95 crosses baseline + X sigma; X tuned to reduce false positives observed in staging.

Backwards compatibility: This is additive and non-breaking for any existing dashboards/alerts. Metrics use new metric names and tags; old metrics remain unchanged.

review_comments: Miguel Sanchez: Nice work. Two questions: (1) Are we confident the token_position buckets are the right granularity? We saw noise in staging after increasing retention. (2) Please add an explanation in the docs about why we hash customer ids and how to map to real customer ids for internal on-call only.

Asha Patel: Re: buckets — we iterated on buckets in staging; the chosen buckets reduced cardinaility while preserving first-token vs mid-token behavior. Added note in docs with the staging experiment results (see commit e5910ab). Re: customer id hashing — added an appendix that explains the internal mapping process locked behind RBAC.
Priya Kapoor: Alert tuning looks reasonable. For the token-cost spike alert, can we add a 2-minute suppression window when the model-variant is in warmup to avoid startup noise?
Asha Patel: Added suppression for model-variant warmup; rule now ignores spikes tagged with model_variant_status=warmup for 2m (commit c3d2e4b).
Jordan McIntyre: Can we add a quick Grafana link that pre-filters by route/model in our Console integration?
Asha Patel: Added pre-filtering support and a Console component to compose linkified dashboard views (redwood-console changes).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash. Merge commit: 6f7a2b3 (squash) — title rewritten to follow conventional commit style. Backport scheduled to release/2026-02 in a follow-up PR.
release_notes: Add token-level cost and latency observability: new token.generate.* metrics, Grafana dashboard (Token Cost & Latency), Prometheus recording rules, and tuned alerts to detect cost/latency regressions. Docs updated with interpretation guide and Console quickstart.
